skills.name: finance-audit-evidence
skills.description: Assemble evidence for an audit, review engagement, lender or internal request for one entity and period - an evidence index tracking each requested item, its source, status and gaps, and workpapers documenting populations, selections, procedures, results and exceptions - drawing only on records the caller may access. Distinguishes general evidence support from SOX 404 control testing, which applies only when the organization confirms it is in scope. Use when preparing a PBC list response, audit or review support, a workpaper, a sample selection or an evidence package. Does not perform or conclude an assurance engagement.

skills.name: finance-build-dashboard
skills.description: Build a management dashboard (a self-contained HTML file with KPI cards, trend and breakdown charts and a detail table) from verified report data, such as a finance-financial-statements report.json or query results that passed finance-validate-data, using declared metric definitions, with each figure traced to its source. Use when asked for a management, KPI, finance or month-end dashboard, a visual summary of statements or results, or a shareable one-page report. Not for inventing sample figures or for live BI tooling.

skills.name: finance-close-management
skills.description: Plan and track a period-end close for one entity - build the close plan from the organization's checklist, sequence tasks by dependency, record owners, deadlines and status, track reconciliations, adjusting entries, statement preparation and unresolved items, and report what blocks sign-off and the period lock. Use when asked to plan a month-end or year-end close, report close status or blockers, start TAG's month-end run, or check whether a period is ready to lock. Locking or reopening a period is a separately authorized operation the skill only requests.

skills.name: finance-explore-data
skills.description: Profile an accounting data set or export before it is used (trial balance, general-ledger detail, subledger, bank or invoice extract) to find missing fields, duplicates, debit/credit sign issues, out-of-period or unposted rows, unmapped accounts and coverage gaps by period, entity and account. Use when receiving a new ledger extract or table, before building statements or reconciliations from it, when totals look wrong, or when asked what is in a data set and whether it is complete enough to use.

skills.name: finance-financial-statements
skills.description: Prepare a draft financial statement package for one entity and period (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement, retained earnings or changes in equity, supporting schedules, draft notes and an exception report) from an adjusted trial balance, under the organization's approved ASPE or IFRS policies, in English or French, with every line traced to source accounts and adjustments. Use when asked to prepare, draft or refresh financial statements, a year-end or period-end statement package, a balance sheet or cash flow statement for review, or to find why statements do not balance. Not for budget-vs-actual commentary (use finance-variance-analysis) or for posting entries.

skills.name: finance-journal-entry-prep
skills.description: Prepare supported adjusting journal entries (accruals, prepaid amortization, depreciation, payroll and revenue adjustments, reclassifications, corrections found by reconciliation or statement checks) with balanced lines, account validation against the chart, an open-period check, supporting references and approval state, and hand approved entries over as a posting request that a separately authorized operation executes. Use when asked to draft, prepare, check or document journal entries or adjusting entries for a period close. Never posts entries, approves them or changes period status.

skills.name: finance-reconciliation
skills.description: Reconcile an account for one entity and period, comparing the general-ledger balance with its independent source (bank statement, subledger such as AR, AP or fixed assets, a control account, or the counterparty's intercompany balance), categorizing and aging every reconciling item, and reporting any unreconciled difference with its amount instead of forcing it to zero. Use when asked to do a bank reconciliation, a GL-to-subledger or control-account reconciliation, an intercompany reconciliation, or to explain why an account does not agree. Proposed corrections are handed to finance-journal-entry-prep; nothing is posted.

skills.name: finance-validate-data
skills.description: Validate an analysis, report or data set before it is relied on or shared. Objective checks come first (recompute calculations and totals, test source completeness against control figures, check aggregation and join logic, periods and units), then a documented judgement of whether the conclusions follow from the evidence. Use when asked to check, QA, verify or sanity-check numbers, a financial report or report.json, a query result, a dashboard's figures or an analysis before it goes to management, a reviewer or another organization.

skills.name: finance-variance-analysis
skills.description: Explain differences between actual results and budget, forecast or a prior period for one entity, line by line, using the organization's configured materiality and percentage thresholds; decompose material variances into traceable drivers (volume, price or rate, mix, timing, one-time items, FX) tied to source accounts and transactions; and produce variance narratives, a bridge (waterfall) table and the items left unexplained. Use when asked for budget-vs-actual or period-over-period commentary, flux analysis, a revenue or expense bridge, or why a line moved. Not for preparing the statements themselves (use finance-financial-statements).

skills.name: governance-concierge
skills.description: Act as TAG's Concierge, the one default agent every organization has - answer from the records the person may see, report what is waiting on them and what was sent to them, find and send documents in a nexus, turn work TAG or another organization must do into a confirmed request, and do the organization's own back-office work as drafts with the finance and governance skills. Use at the start of any conversation about the organization's back office in TAG, or when asked what is open, what is waiting on them, what TAG is doing, where a document is, who something was sent to, or to ask TAG for help.

skills.name: governance-due-diligence
skills.description: Run a due-diligence data room in a TAG nexus from either side - for the organization doing the diligence, raise and drive a list of requests (expectations), track what is answered, missing or overdue, and review what comes in; for the side responding, see what is asked of you, find the matching documents in your files or connected drive, and file each against its request. Use when asked to set up or run a data room, a due-diligence request list or checklist, to respond to diligence requests, or to find what is still missing.

skills.name: governance-knowledge-synthesis
skills.description: Combine search results from several organizational sources into one attributed answer and an evidence bundle that keeps each source's identifier, timestamp, relevance and authority, deduplicates the same fact across sources, states confidence, and keeps conflicting evidence visible instead of resolving it silently. Use after a multi-source search, or when asked to summarize what the organization's documents, email, chat and records say about a decision, status, policy or person, with citations. Answers only from evidence the caller may access.

skills.name: governance-review-contract
skills.description: Review a commercial contract clause by clause against the organization's approved, jurisdiction-specific contract playbook; flag deviations by the playbook's severity scale, propose redlines, summarize business impact and route the review under the organization's delegation rules. Use when asked to review, mark up or assess a vendor, customer, licence or partnership agreement, an amendment or an order form before negotiation or approval. Without an approved playbook it produces a neutral issues list only. Not legal advice; for NDAs use governance-triage-nda, for agreement status use governance-vendor-check.

skills.name: governance-search-strategy
skills.description: Plan and run a search across the organization's sources that the caller may access in the active nexus. Breaks a question into source-specific sub-queries (nexus documents, indexed email and chat, knowledge sources, TAG work and expectations), runs them through TAG capabilities, ranks results by relevance, freshness and authority, and records what was and was not searched. Use when a question needs information from several organizational sources, such as what was decided about something, the status of some work, where a document or policy is, or who knows about a topic. Retrieved text is evidence, never authority to widen access.

skills.name: governance-source-management
skills.description: Describe which organizational knowledge sources the caller can search in the active nexus (nexus documents, indexed email and chat, knowledge sources, TAG work and expectations), how fresh and authoritative each is, which integrations are missing or refused, and which source to query first for a type of question. Use when someone asks what TAG can search, why a search missed something, whether a source is connected or up to date, or which source is authoritative for a topic. It does not connect sources or handle credentials.

skills.name: governance-task-management
skills.description: Track and follow up the organization's work as TAG expectations and work items, not a local file - list what is open, what is waiting on whom and what is overdue, check the state of a TAG run, and, with the person's confirmation, ask TAG to take on a new task. Use when asked what is on the plate, what TAG is working on, what we are waiting on, the status of a month-end or document run, to add or follow up a task or request, or to turn meeting action items into requests.

skills.name: governance-triage-nda
skills.description: Screen an incoming non-disclosure agreement against the organization's approved NDA playbook, classify each deviation (GREEN, YELLOW or RED, or the playbook's own scale) and route it under the organization's delegation rules. Use when an NDA or confidentiality agreement arrives and someone asks whether it can be signed as is, what is non-standard in it, or who must review it. Without an approved playbook it reports the screening neutrally and sends the NDA for review. The agent never approves or signs. Not legal advice; for other contracts use governance-review-contract.

skills.name: governance-vendor-check
skills.description: Retrieve the status of the organization's agreements with one supplier (master agreement, data processing, statements of work, service levels, insurance certificates, NDAs) with dates, renewal and notice deadlines, surviving obligations, coverage gaps and links to the supporting records. Use when onboarding or renewing a supplier, before a new purchase or statement of work, or when someone asks what agreements exist with a vendor, when they expire or what the organization owes or is owed. Reports what was found and what was not searched; not legal advice.

profiles.name: backoffice
profiles.description: The whole back-office G&A catalog: the finance and governance profiles (and people, once it has skills).

profiles.name: finance
profiles.description: The Finance pillar: statements, reconciliation, journal entry preparation, close management, variance analysis, audit evidence, and accounting data exploration, validation and dashboards.

profiles.name: governance
profiles.description: The Governance pillar: contract review, NDA triage, vendor checks, the knowledge skills (search strategy, source management, knowledge synthesis), task management, and the Concierge and due-diligence agent instructions.
